steps.prompt:
Create original photographic artwork for the Carrel infrastructure product, part of the zyx Made series. Contemporary Japanese and Korean editorial photography, natural physical materials, restrained styling, calm ordinary study spaces with one unexpected geometric object. Carrel's object is a cobalt blue glazed ceramic squared arch, shaped like an inverted U with thick rounded edges, two straight vertical legs, one wide horizontal top bridge, and an open rectangular void reaching the floor. Keep this exact silhouette consistent. No text, letters, logos, watermarks, signage, labels, arrows, diagrams, captions, interface, collage, borders or graphic bands. Soft directional daylight, gentle direct flash, subtle lens softness, realistic details. The final images will receive film grain in postproduction, do not exaggerate noise.

Use case: product-mockup. A single freestanding oversized cobalt ceramic squared arch sculpture on a quiet pale warm-gray seamless floor. Three-quarter frontal view, modest depth, rounded edges and believable glossy ceramic reflections, slightly imperfect glaze. Exact shape: one wide flat top bridge and two parallel legs, all connected, an inverted squared U with a fully open bottom. Outer top corners softly rounded. Center it, fill 70 percent of the square frame, with generous breathing room and soft cast shadow. Elegant physical object photography, no other objects, no people. Deep blue glaze, no metallic chrome, no text.

Use case: photorealistic-natural. Reference 1 defines the exact cobalt ceramic arch. Reference 2 defines only the series' photographic mood, not the subject identity or setting. Cast a distinct original adult East Asian woman age 27 with a chin-length black bob, natural face and calm direct gaze, wearing a plain pale-gray cotton shirt and charcoal trousers. She sits in a quiet old university library study carrel, on a simple oak chair, casually resting one forearm on a huge cobalt ceramic arch standing on the desk beside her. The arch is about the size of her upper body, its two feet rest naturally on the tabletop and its open bottom is fully visible. Her face and hands are clear and anatomically correct. One closed unmarked cream book on the desk. Photograph from a few meters back with a 35mm lens, environmental portrait. Place the woman and sculpture within the LEFT 57 percent of the frame. The RIGHT 38 percent is uninterrupted softly lit cream plaster wall for website text. Pale quiet top edge. Warm oak table, subtle blue reflections, ordinary library atmosphere, no visible writing on book spines. Make the entire frame one continuous real photograph. No text or UI.

The cobalt glazed ceramic squared arch must remain completely rigid and stationary, preserving its two legs, wide top bridge, open bottom, thickness, glazing, reflections and contact points. Keep the oak desk, chair, hands, book, clothing and cream wall unchanged. No zoom, camera move, reframing, text or added objects. Settle into the exact reference pose at the end for a quiet loop.
